genotype_structure_note: Heterozygous pathogenic variants; do not assume HBB-style recessive homozygous genotypes.

diseases.label: Coffin-Siris syndrome 1 (CSS1)
diseases.genotype_scope: Heterozygous pathogenic ARID1B variant in a person meeting CSS clinical criteria
diseases.notes: Gene-defined CSS subtype. Other BAF-complex genes can cause CSS clinically; keep ARID1B-CSS1 distinct from CSS caused by other genes.

diseases.label: ARID1B-related disorder (ARID1B-RD)
diseases.notes: Gene-centered clinical umbrella used by FAR/CARE4ARID1B for the spectrum from CSS-like presentations to less syndromic intellectual disability. Not a mechanistic proof that every presentation shares identical modifiers.

diseases.label: ARID1B-related nonsyndromic intellectual disability
diseases.omim_related: OMIM:614562 (MRD12 / historical labels may appear in sources)
diseases.notes: Keep separate from CSS1. Same gene, overlapping variant classes, different clinical framing; van der Sluijs et al. compare CSS-ascertained vs ID-ascertained cohorts.

representative_variants.notes: Representative ClinVar pathogenic nonsense allele. Predicted molecular consequence ≠ experimentally measured functional effect for every carrier context.

representative_variants.experimental_effect: Donor splice disruption with exon 17 skipping leading to frameshift (reported RNA studies)
representative_variants.notes: Synonymous-looking coding change with splice effect — illustrates predicted vs experimentally observed consequence distinction.

inclusion_criteria: Germline ARID1B monogenic neurodevelopmental presentations with public primary sources
Edges require source URL + supporting passage or structured-field reference
Keep CSS1, ARID1B-RD umbrella, and nonsyndromic ID labels distinct
exclusion_criteria: Somatic cancer associations for ARID1B/BAF subunits as if they were the germline rare-disease mechanism
Claims that every truncating variant has proven functional protein loss without context
Approved gene-therapy or disease-modifying treatment claims
Cross-links to HBB hemoglobinopathy nodes without a supporting source
